children: SYDNEY--Australian services-sector activity continued to expand solidly in August, underscoring the resilience of the economy in the face of continuing global shocks and rising interest rates.
The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Australia Services PMI business activity index posted 53.2 in August, a touch lower than the reading of 53.6 in July.
"The latest expansions in business activity and new orders were solid but unspectacular," Andrew Harker, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said.
"Rising business confidence and reports of strong pipelines of new work hint at improving growth rates in the months ahead," he added.

The data comes a day after second-quarter economic-growth data came in stronger than expected, stoking the case for the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise interest rates further, perhaps as early as later this month.
The services sector recorded a second successive monthly rise in new orders, while business confidence rose to a six-month high and employment expanded, the data showed.

There were again widespread reports of higher costs for fuel and staff, resulting in a further sharp increase in input prices, but companies raised their selling prices at a softer pace, according to the report.
Services-sector activity has now risen in three consecutive months with the exception being information and communication.
The rise in overall new business was recorded in spite of a further reduction in new export orders--the fourth in as many months, the report said.

High fuel costs and lower tourist numbers reportedly caused the latest fall in new business from abroad, which was nonetheless the least pronounced in the current sequence of decline, the data showed.
